{{nihongo|'''Hakozaki Shrine'''|筥崎宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Chikuzen Province]].

'''Hakozaki-gū''' (はこざきぐう) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Hakozaki|ja|箱崎 (福岡市)|qid=Q11603321|lt=Hakozaki}}, {{ill|Higashi-ku, Fukuoka|ceb|Higashi Ku (subdistrito sa Hapon, Fukuoka-ken)|cs|Higaši-ku (Fukuoka)|es|Higashi-ku (Fukuoka)|fa|هیگاشی-کو، فوکوئوکا|fi|Higashi-ku (Fukuoka)|fr|Higashi-ku (Fukuoka)|id|Higashi-ku, Fukuoka|it|Higashi-ku (Fukuoka)|ja|東区 (福岡市)|ko|히가시구 (후쿠오카시)|pl|Higashi (Fukuoka)|th|เขตฮิงาชิ (ฟูกูโอกะ)|tr|Higashi, Fukuoka|ur|ہیگاشی وارڈ، فوکوکا|vi|Higashi, Fukuoka|zh|東區 (福岡市)|zh_yue|東區 (福岡市)|qid=Q1206659|lt=Higashi Ward}}, {{ill|Fukuoka|Q26600|qid=Q26600}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and an {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|qid=Q1047664}}{{Efn|Together with {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)|Q29682|qid=Q29682|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} in Sumiyoshi, {{ill|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|ar|هاكاتا-كو|ceb|Hakata Ku|cs|Hakata-ku (Fukuoka)|es|Hakata-ku (Fukuoka)|fa|هاکاتا-کو، فوکوئوکا|fi|Hakata-ku|fr|Hakata-ku|hu|Hakata|id|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|it|Hakata-ku|ja|博多区|ko|하카타구|pl|Hakata (Fukuoka)|pt|Hakata|th|เขตฮากาตะ|tr|Hakata|ur|ہاکاتا وارڈ، فوکوکا|vi|Hakata, Fukuoka|zh|博多區|zh_yue|博多區|qid=Q1330839}}.}}. Its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}, and it is now a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

It is also called '''Hakozaki Hachimangū''' (はこざきはちまんぐう). Together with {{ill|Usa Jingū|de|Usa Hachiman-gū|el|Ούσα Τζίνγκου|eu|Usa jingū|fr|Usa Hachiman-gū|id|Kuil Usa|ja|宇佐神宮|ko|우사 신궁|la|Usa-jingū|or|ଉସାଜିଙ୍ଗୁ|ru|Уса-дзингу|simple|Usa Jingū|tok|tomo sewi suli Usa|tr|Usa Jingū|zh|宇佐神宮|qid=Q715632}} in {{ill|Usa, Ōita|Q114147|qid=Q114147}}, {{ill|Ōita Prefecture|Q133924|qid=Q133924}}, and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}} in {{ill|Yawata|Q260923|qid=Q260923}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}, it is called one of the '''{{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637|lt=Three Great Hachiman Shrines}}'''{{Efn|In popular usage, the “Three Great Hachiman” usually means “Usa Jingū and Iwashimizu Hachimangū,” plus either this shrine or {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|Q701403|qid=Q701403}}. In late-Edo to Meiji materials, the three examples listed in the Daijō-kan notice dated old-calendar {{ill|April 24 (Lunisolar)|cdo|4 nguŏk 24 hô̤ (nùng-lĭk)|ja|4月24日 (旧暦)|ko|음력 4월 24일|zh|四月廿四|zh_min_nan|4 goe̍h 24 ji̍t (kū-le̍k)|zh_yue|四月廿四|qid=Q839640}}<ref>{{Cite book |ja|author=Tanaka Tsunekiyo |title=Mysterious God: Everything about Hachiman, as told by the chief priest of Iwashimizu Hachimangū |publisher=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha |date=2010-03 |isbn=4404038291 |page=198}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.d1.dion.ne.jp/~s_minaga/s_tatu.htm |title=Shinbutsu Bunri Order |website=Shinbutsu Bunri, or Haibutsu Kishaku |access-date=2015-12-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081030054401/https://www.d1.dion.ne.jp/~s_minaga/s_tatu.htm |archive-date=2008-10-30}}{{信頼性要検証|date=2024-11}}</ref> and ranked as Kanpei Taisha were “Usa, Iwashimizu, Hakozaki”; however, some recent books present “Usa, Iwashimizu, Tsurugaoka” as representative Hachiman shrines<ref>{{Cite book |ja |title=National Directory of Hachiman Shrines |publisher=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha |series=Bessatsu Rekishi Dokuhon 99 Shrine Series 3| date=2004-11 |isbn=4404030991 |page=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |ja |author=Shirai Eiji |author2=Toki Masanori |title=Shrine Dictionary |edition=New popular edition |publisher=Tōkyōdō Shuppan |date=1997-09 |isbn=449010474X |page=}}</ref>.}}.

=== Shrine name ===
The proper character for “hako” is 「筥」 (a cylindrical container), not 「箱」. However, for place names, station names, etc., {{要出典範囲|the toponym “hakozaki” is written as 「箱崎」 rather than the shrine’s 「筥崎」 out of reverence for the Hakozaki Hachiman deity.|date=2023-03}}

=== History ===
[[File:箱崎八幡宮縁起.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Origin account of Hakozaki Hachimangū]]

There are multiple theories regarding its founding<ref name="history">{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/history/ |title=History of Hakozaki-gū |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref><ref name="tsuchida">{{Cite journal |ja |author=Mitsuyoshi Tsuchida |year=1972 |title=On the architecture of the main sanctuary of Hakozaki Hachimangū |journal=Transactions of the Architectural Institute of Japan |volume=195 |pages=69-74,98 |publisher=Architectural Institute of Japan |crid=1390001205537700736| doi=10.3130/aijsaxx.195.0_69}}</ref>; the official site introduces the theory that it was established in {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} 21<ref name="history" />. On June 21 of Engi 21 ({{ill|921|ab|921|af|921|am|921 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|921|ar|921|ary|921|ast|921|avk|921|az|921|azb|۹۲۱ (میلادی)|bcl|921|be|921|be_x_old|921|bg|921|bn|৯২১|bpy|মারি ৯২১|br|921|bs|921.|ca|921|cdo|921 nièng|ce|921 шо|ceb|921|ckb|٩٢١|crh|921|cs|921|csb|921|cv|921|cy|921|da|921|de|921|el|921|eml|921|eo|921|es|921|et|921|eu|921|fa|۹۲۱ (میلادی)|fi|921|fo|921|fr|921|fy|921|ga|921|gan|921年|gd|921|gl|921|he|921|hi|921|hr|921.|ht|921 (almanak jilyen)|hu|921|hy|921|id|921|ilo|921|io|921|is|921|it|921|ja|921年|jv|921|ka|921|kaa|921|kk|921 жыл|ko|921년|la|921|lb|921|lij|921|lmo|921|lt|921 m.|lv|921. gads|map_bms|921|mdf|921|mg|921|mhr|921|mi|921|mk|921|mr|इ.स. ९२१|mrj|921 и|ms|921|mzn|۹۲۱|nah|921|nap|921|nds|921|new|सन् ९२१|nl|921|nn|921|no|921|nrm|921|nso|921|oc|921|or|୯୨୧|os|921-æм аз|pl|921|pnb|921|pt|921|qu|921|ro|921|ru|921 год|rue|921|sa|९२१|scn|921|sd|921ع|se|921|sh|921.|shn|921|si|921|sk|921|sl|921|smn|921|sq|921|sr|921|su|921|sv|921|sw|921|tg|Соли 921|th|พ.ศ. 1464|tk|921|tl|921|tly|921|tr|921|tt|921 ел|uk|921|ur|921ء|uz|921|vec|921|vi|921|vls|921|war|921|wuu|921年|xmf|921|zh|921年|zh_min_nan|921 nî|zh_yue|921年|qid=Q30102}}), there was an oracle from {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}}, and it began when Ōjin, Jingū, and Tamayori-hime were enshrined by relocating {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daibumiya}} in {{ill|Honami district|Q11597062|qid=Q11597062}}, Chikuzen Province, to land facing the {{ill|Genkai Sea|Q498047|qid=Q498047}}<ref name="history" />. In {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 1 ({{ill|923|Q30108|qid=Q30108}}), it was transferred to the current site<ref name="history" />. In the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' it is listed as “Hachiman Daibosatsu Hakozaki-gū, one seat,” and ranked as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}.

During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|Q208156|qid=Q208156}}, retired emperor {{ill|Emperor Kameyama|Q360972|qid=Q360972|lt=Kameyama Jōkō}} prayed for the enemy’s submission; a copy of his writing was made in the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|ar|فترة أزوتشي-موموياما|ast|Periodu Azuchi-Momoyama|be|Перыяд Адзуці-Мамаяма|bg|Адзучи-Момояма|br|Marevezh Azuchi-Momoyama|ca|Període Azuchi-Momoyama|ckb|سەردەمی ئازوچی-مۆمۆیاما|cs|Období Azuči-Momojama|de|Azuchi-Momoyama-Zeit|eo|Azuĉi-Momojama-epoko|es|Período Azuchi-Momoyama|eu|Azuchi-Momoyama aroa|fa|دوره آزوچی-مومویاما|fi|Azuchi-Momoyama-kausi|fr|Époque Azuchi Momoyama|he|תקופת אזוצ'י-מומויאמה|hu|Azucsi–Momojama-kor|id|Zaman Azuchi–Momoyama|it|Periodo Azuchi-Momoyama|ja|安土桃山時代|ka|აძუტი-მომოიამა|ko|아즈치모모야마 시대|lt|Momojama laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Azuchi–Momoyama|nl|Azuchi-Momoyamaperiode|no|Azuchi-Momoyama-perioden|pl|Azuchi-Momoyama|pt|Período Azuchi-Momoyama|ro|Perioada Azuchi-Momoyama|ru|Период Адзути-Момояма|simple|Azuchi–Momoyama period|sk|Obdobie Azuči-Momojama|sr|Азучи-Момојама период|sv|Azuchi|th|ยุคอาซูจิ–โมโมยามะ|tl|Panahong Azuchi–Momoyama|tr|Azuchi-Momoyama Dönemi|uk|Період Адзуті-Момояма|vi|Thời kỳ Azuchi-Momoyama|wuu|安土桃山时代|zh|安土桃山时代|zh_min_nan|Azuti-Momoyama sî-tāi|zh_yue|安土桃山時代|qid=Q319531}} and displayed on the shrine gate as a {{ill|biane|Q5358873|qid=Q5358873}} reading “敵國降伏” (submission of enemy countries)<ref name="history" />. Since then, it has been worshipped as a deity of maritime traffic and overseas defense.

Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}, it was ranked as a prefectural shrine in Meiji 4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}). It was promoted to Kanpei Chūsha in {{ill|1885|Q7821|qid=Q7821}} (Meiji 18), and to Kanpei Taisha in {{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}} (Taishō 3)<ref name="history" />.

=== Precincts ===
The main buildings and facilities in the precincts are as follows.
* Main sanctuary and worship hall
** Important Cultural Property. Founded in June 921 (Engi 21) by Fujiwara no Mazai. Repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt multiple times<ref name="tsuchida" />. It fell into ruin due to warfare in the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023}}, and was rebuilt in {{ill|Tenbun|ckb|تێنبون|fa|تنبون|fi|Tenbun-kausi|fr|Ère Tenbun|it|Tenbun|ja|天文 (元号)|ko|덴분|pt|Tenbun|ru|Тэмбун|simple|Tenbun|sr|Тенбун|sv|Tenbun|tr|Tenbun|zh|天文 (日本)|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 15 (1546) by Dazai Daini {{ill|Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Q1065163|qid=Q1065163}}<ref name="tsuchida" />. The main sanctuary is 46 tsubo, {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} style with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hiwada-buki}} roof, with side carriage porches<ref name="keidai">{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/keidai/ |title=Guide to the precincts |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>. The worship hall is {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} with cypress bark roofing<ref name="keidai" />, double {{ill|kōryō|Q124421222|qid=Q124421222}}, and {{ill|kaerumata|Q123117911|qid=Q123117911}}.
* Rōmon gate
** Important Cultural Property. Built in {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} 3 ({{ill|1594|Q6777|qid=Q6777}}) by {{ill|Kobayakawa Takakage|Q1143508|qid=Q1143508}}<ref name="keidai" />. Three-bay, one-door {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}<ref name="keidai" />. The paulownia crest carving on the doors is said to be by {{ill|Hidari Jingorō|Q2668220|qid=Q2668220}}<ref name="keidai" />. The “Enemy Country Submission” {{ill|biane|Q5358873|qid=Q5358873}} is said to be an imperial inscription by {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}} donated by {{ill|Emperor Kameyama|Q360972|qid=Q360972}}. “Fukuteki-mon” in {{ill|Hirose Tansō|Q1620267|qid=Q1620267}}’s poem “Chikuzen Jōka-saku” refers to this gate. General worship is performed under this rōmon. It is counted as one of Japan’s three great rōmon.
* Stone First Torii (Hizen Torii)
** Important Cultural Property. Long said to have been erected in {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 14 ({{ill|1609|Q6762|qid=Q6762}}) by {{ill|Kuroda Nagamasa|Q950496|qid=Q950496}}<ref name="keidai" />, but Sasebo City cultural property examiner Hisamura Sadao established that it was erected by {{ill|Saga Domain|Q2975995|qid=Q2975995}} lord {{ill|Nabeshima Katsushige|Q3138980|qid=Q3138980}}<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/1008063 |title=Returning a favor to Kuroda Nagamasa in “Sekigahara” links: National Important Cultural Property “Hakozaki Torii” may have been donated by the Nabeshima clan {{!}} Administration/Society {{!}} Saga Shimbun News |website=Saga Shimbun |publisher=Saga Shimbunsha |date=2024-05-08 |access-date=2024-05-08}}</ref>. The torii pillars are made in three sections, bulging downward and continuing into base stones<ref name="keidai" />. The kasagi and shimaki are one stone piece, with upturned tips, and equal lengths of nuki and kasagi—typical '''Hizen torii'''<ref name="keidai" />. The stone used is {{ill|Aō stone|Q109360266|qid=Q109360266}}, a specialty of {{ill|Takashima|Q10860535|qid=Q10860535|lt=Takashima}}, {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|Q169376|qid=Q169376}}<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://tabinaga.jp/column/view.php?category=5&hid=20140226202035 |author=Moriki Matsu |title=The stone industry tradition of Takashima: “Aō stone” |website=Traveling Nagasaki Studies |publisher=Nagasaki Prefectural Cultural Promotion Division |access-date=2021-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506120926/https://tabinaga.jp/column/view.php?category=5&hid=20140226202035 |archive-date=2021-05-06}}</ref>. Calling it “Hakozaki torii” is incorrect.
* Stone lantern
** Important Cultural Property. Of many stone lanterns, one with an inscription dated {{ill|Kannō|Q1145053|qid=Q1145053}} 1 ({{ill|1350|Q6094|qid=Q6094}}) on the underside of the fire box is said to have been donated by {{ill|Sen no Rikyū|Q305477|qid=Q305477}} in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 15 ({{ill|1587|Q6744|qid=Q6744}}).
* Sacred tree “Hako-matsu”
** A pine tree on the right of the rōmon enclosed by a red {{ill|Sacred fences|Q3078312|qid=Q3078312}} fence<ref name="keidai" />. It is said that when {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} gave birth to {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, the {{ill|Placenta|Q1212935|qid=Q1212935|lt=ena}} was put in a box and buried, and this sacred pine was planted as a marker<ref name="keidai" />. The name “Hakozaki” derives from that box containing the placenta<ref name="keidai" />.
* Karafune-tō
* Yūshutsu-seki
* Shrine garden Hanateien{{Efn|Location: Maidashi 4-chome, external link: <ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/hanameguri/ |title=Approach flower tour |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2022-11-21}}</ref>}}
* {{読み仮名|Tall Lantern|たかとうろう}}{{Efn|Location: Hakozaki 2-chome 55 {{Coord|33|37|1.86|N|130|25|0.17|E}}. Summary of local signboard: “A stone lantern about 6 meters tall. First built in {{ill|1817|Q6958|qid=Q6958}} (Bunka 14) by fishermen of Hakozaki-ura as a landmark for returning from fishing in {{ill|Hakata Bay|ceb|Hakata Wan|cs|Zátoka Hakata|fa|خلیج هاکاتا|fi|Hakatanlahti|fr|Baie de Hakata|it|Baia di Hakata|ja|博多湾|ko|하카타만|ms|Teluk Hakata|pl|Hakata (zatoka)|sv|Hakatabukten|qid=Q2344806}}. In {{ill|1882|Q7812|qid=Q7812}} (Meiji 15) it was moved to the present location, then at the shoreline, and its upper part was changed from wood to stone. It was repaired again in {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}} (Shōwa 43).”<ref>{{Cite report |df=ja |author=Fukuoka City Higashi Ward Office / Hakozaki school district council |title=Tall Lantern |location=Hakozaki 2-chome 55 |at=Signboard (onsite)}}</ref>. External link: <ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/ |title=Fukuoka City Cultural Properties |publisher=Fukuoka City Bureau of Economy, Tourism and Culture, Cultural Properties Utilization Division |access-date=2022-11-22}} → cultural property search → keyword search</ref>}}
* {{読み仮名|Hakozaki-gū Hamamiya|はこざきぐうはまみや}}{{Efn|Location: Hakozaki 2-chome 55 {{Coord|33|37|2.06|N|130|25|2.01|E}}, alias: traffic safety prayer hall (large vehicles)}}

Also, a long approach of about 850 meters continues from the first torii facing {{ill|Hakata Bay|ceb|Hakata Wan|cs|Zátoka Hakata|fa|خلیج هاکاتا|fi|Hakatanlahti|fr|Baie de Hakata|it|Baia di Hakata|ja|博多湾|ko|하카타만|ms|Teluk Hakata|pl|Hakata (zatoka)|sv|Hakatabukten|qid=Q2344806}} to the main sanctuary. The Hakozaki-hama area in front of the approach formerly had a beautiful {{ill|Coast|Q93352|qid=Q93352|lt=coast}} praised as {{ill|white sands and green pines|Q11580253|qid=Q11580253}}, but harbor works for Hakata Port brought seawall development by {{ill|1936|Q18649|qid=Q18649}}, and today the area has changed drastically, with {{ill|Hakozaki Futō|Q110985033|qid=Q110985033}} to the north and {{ill|Higashihama|Q110970101|qid=Q110970101|lt=Higashihama}} (Higashihama Wharf) and Hakata Port warehouses to the south. The beach beyond the approach is maintained as sandy ground so people can perform “Oshioi-tori,” receiving purifying {{読み仮名|{{ill|Decomposed granite|Q3275386|qid=Q3275386|lt=sand}}|まさご}}. Hakozaki-hama is adjacent to Hakozaki boat basin{{Efn|Hakozaki boat basin is not a {{ill|fishing port|Q1420027|qid=Q1420027}} designated under the {{ill|Act on Development of Fishing Ports and Grounds|Q11565358|qid=Q11565358}}; it corresponds to “{{ill|basin for small craft|Q106835724|qid=Q106835724}},” one of the water-area facilities defined in Article 2, Paragraph 5, Item 1 of the Port and Harbor Act. One corner also has the {{ill|Fukuoka Fisheries Cooperative|Q11592233|qid=Q11592233|lt=Hakozaki Branch}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Fisheries Cooperative|Q11592233|qid=Q11592233}}.}}. Besides the first torii in front of the main hall, there is a second torii near the intersection of the approach and the Nishitetsu bus-only road (Nishitetsu Hakozaki bus stop / Subway Hakozaki-miyamae Station Exit 1). A large torii built in 1930 once stood at the intersection of the seaward {{ill|Japan National Route 3|Q1138454|qid=Q1138454}} and the approach, but it was dismantled and removed between March and April 2018 due to risk of mortar detachment from deterioration.

=== Major festivals ===
* January 3: Tamaseseri (Ball-Grabbing Festival)<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/tamatorisai/ |title=Tamaseseri |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
** Men in {{ill|Fundoshi|Q976963|qid=Q976963|lt=shimekomi}} attire struggle over a wooden sacred jewel (said to grant good fortune) and offer it into the main hall.
* January 11: Jōtenji Ichizan Hōsaishiki<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/jotenjiichizanhousaishiki/ |title=Jōtenji Ichizan Hōsaishiki |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
** Monks of {{ill|Jōten-ji|Q3191242|qid=Q3191242}} chant sutras before the deity in gratitude, because Shōichi Kokushi {{ill|Enni|Q739826|qid=Q739826}} (Ben’en), when returning from Song China, survived maritime danger by protection of Hakozaki Hachiman.
* Day of Tsuchinoe nearest spring equinox: Spring Shani-sai (Oshioi-tori)<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/shunkishanichisai/ |title=Spring Shani-sai / Oshioi-tori |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
** Purifying sand is received at Hakozaki-hama and scattered at homes and fields for household safety and good harvest.
* Late June: Ikeshima-dono Grand Festival<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/ikeshimadensai/ |title=Ikeshima-dono Festival |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
* July 1 and 9: Oshioi-tori
** Carriers of the {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|Q1749262|qid=Q1749262}} take sand at Hakozaki-hama for purification.
* July 7: Tanabata Festival<ref>{{Cite web |ja|url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/tanabatasai/ |title=Tanabata Festival |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
* Late July: Nagoshi Festival<ref>{{Cite web |ja|url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/nagoshisai/ |title=Nagoshi Festival / Chinowa passage |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
* September 12–18: {{読み仮名|{{ill|Hōjōya|ja|放生会 (筥崎宮)|qid=Q67704099|lt=Hōjō-e}}|ほうじょうや}}<ref name="houjoya">{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/houjoya/ |title=Hōjō-e |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
** Festival honoring life and giving thanks for blessings of sea and mountains<ref name="houjoya" />. Considered one of Hakata’s three great festivals<ref name="houjoya" />. Unglazed-clay {{ill|Ohajiki|Q11262088|qid=Q11262088}} and glass noisemaker toys “chanpon” ({{ill|bidoro|Q11278090|qid=Q11278090|lt=bidoro}}, {{ill|poppen|Q11278090|qid=Q11278090|lt=poppen}}) are sold. Various stalls line the 1-{{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224}} approach. In Hakata it is affectionately called “pear and persimmon season is Hōjō-e.” {{要出典範囲|date=2017-09|Generally “放生会” is read “hōjō'''e'''”, but}} at Hakozaki-gū and especially in Fukuoka it is traditionally read “hōjō'''ya'''” to distinguish it from Buddhist events read “hōjōe”<ref name="houjoya" />.
* Day of Tsuchinoe nearest autumn equinox: Autumn Shani-sai (Oshioi-tori)<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/shukishanichisai/ |title=Autumn Shani-sai / Oshioi-tori |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>
* December 31: Oena Festival (Great Purification, sea-cucumber mochi pounding)<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.hakozakigu.or.jp/omatsuri/ |title=Festivals |publisher=Hakozaki-gū |access-date=2017-09-09}}</ref>

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties (national) ===
* Main sanctuary - Built in late Muromachi period (1545). Nine-bay nagare-zukuri, cypress bark roof. Designated May 27, 1907.
* Worship hall - Built around late Muromachi period (1545). Four bays wide, one bay deep, single-story, kirizuma-zukuri, cypress bark roof. Designated May 27, 1907.
* Rōmon gate - Built in Azuchi–Momoyama period (1573–1614). Three-bay one-door rōmon, irimoya-zukuri, cypress bark roof. Designated April 17, 1902.
* First torii - Built in Azuchi–Momoyama period (1609). Stone myōjin torii. Pillars bear inscription “Keichō 14, year of 己酉, mid-autumn.” Designated June 22, 1955.
* Stone lantern - Built in Nanboku-chō period (1350). Designated February 2, 1962.

=== Imperial-plaque postage stamp of Hakozaki-gū ===
{{double image aside|right|Tejikoku10sen.JPG|120|Inperf 10sen stamp in 1945.JPG|110|Imperial-plaque stamp (1945)<br/>There were perforated (left) and imperforate (right) versions.}}
{{main|Tekikoku Kōfuku stamp}}
As noted above, during the Mongol invasions {{ill|Emperor Kameyama|Q360972|qid=Q360972}} prayed for “submission of enemy countries,” and that plaque hangs on the rōmon. In {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 20), late in the {{ill|Greater East Asia War|Q3846875|qid=Q3846875}} ({{ill|World War II|Q362|qid=Q362}}), the {{ill|Ministry of Communications (Japan)|Q11639479|qid=Q11639479}} (now {{ill|Japan Post Service|Q11509260|qid=Q11509260}}) issued a {{ill|Definitive stamp|Q1002873|qid=Q1002873}} using this plaque design to boost morale and pray for victory. Due to material shortages it was printed in black only, and imperforate versions were also made. However, before it reached post offices nationwide, the war ended, and in {{ill|1947|Q5263|qid=Q5263}} (Shōwa 22), the “Ordinance prohibiting use of postage stamps and postcards whose designs relate to militarism, Shinto, etc.” (1947 Teishin Ministry Ordinance No. 24<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://elaws.e-gov.go.jp/document?lawid=322M40001000024 |title=Ordinance prohibiting use of stamps and postcards whose designs relate to militarism, Shinto, etc. |website=e-Gov law search |access-date=2021-04-21}}</ref>; an ordinance on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=purged stamps}}) banned it from postal use. Even as of {{ill|2021|Q49628|qid=Q49628}} (Reiwa 3), this stamp can still be exchanged for current stamps/postcards at {{ill|Tokyo Central Post Office|Q5153849|qid=Q5153849}} in {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|Q214051|qid=Q214051}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}.
{{See also|Definitive stamps of Japan#Validity of Japanese stamps|Japanese postage stamps#Overview}}
